transcript: Stranger Things: The First Shadow is the latest visual blockbuster to come to Broadway, and I have to admit it was pretty cool. It's pretty much what you'd expect — lots of special effects and surprises within the world of the Netflix series. I haven't seen the show, but since this is a prequel, I don't feel like I missed anything, other than some connections to the events of the series which had a lot of the audience really excited. But it's perfectly fine for a standalone story. The whole experience is a feast for the senses and manages to be pretty big and immersive, even from the rear mezz where I was sitting. If you're sensitive to harsh light and sound, this may not be the show for you as these are frequently dialed up to create some genuine jump scares. I was actually surprised by how much it leans into suspense and horror, and for these reasons, it's not as much of a family show as I had expected. Also, a fair number of jokes are not kid-friendly, though parts of the story I felt were a bit juvenile for how otherwise non-kid-friendly the show is. And the writing itself is kind of lackluster with a slow-progressing plot, but I get why the script needs to stay more surface-level to maintain the fast pace of the overall production. And let's be real — you're not going to this play for the most profound script. You’re probably there for the connection to the beloved series and the visuals, which they do a great job of. I'm not much of a sci-fi person myself, but I do appreciate innovative stagecraft, and this is almost overflowing with it. Also, part of the fun of attending such a visually and practically innovative production is feeling the excitement in the room while everyone's minds are getting blown, and last night there were multiple sequences which were gasp-then-applause-inducing. My last piece of praise would be for Louis McCartney who gives a great leading performance as Henry Creel. His physicality and the ways he shifts between energies throughout the play is really impressive, and the wide array of energies that this production induces, mainly suspense, surprise, and humor, are what make it unforgettable. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Reviewer praises the visuals, stagecraft, and lead performance enthusiastically, but has clear caveats about lackluster writing, slow plot, and tonal inconsistencies. Overall a solid recommendation for the right audience.
